into/ids: A decoder-only language model, the design behind GPT, reads a sequence of T token ids. Here T is four: the, cat, sat, on.
into/embed: First, each id is swapped for its row of the embedding table: T vectors of d numbers, an array of T by d.
into/pos: Attention ignores order, so each position adds a vector of its own, from a table with one row per position. The shape stays T by d.
through/blocks: Then come the transformer blocks, N of them, one after another. Each takes T by d and hands back T by d, so they stack.
through/causal: Every block's attention is causal. Position two sees positions zero, one and two, and never three.
through/why: So no position can peek at the token it will be asked to predict, and all T positions still run at once, in one pass.
out/unembed: At the top, the unembedding scores every vocabulary token at every position: T by d becomes T by V.
out/softmax: A softmax on each row turns those scores into next-token probabilities.
out/shift: Each row predicts the token after its position. Row zero has read the, and predicts cat. Row one predicts sat, and row two predicts on.
out/last: Row three has read the whole sequence, so it predicts the token after all of it: a word not written yet.
out/count: So T tokens give T predictions, all from one forward pass, and training adds up a cross-entropy loss at every position.
